text: China's Silk Road Fund closed its acquisition of a 10% stake in SIBUR in January 2017, with the right to nominate a member of SIBUR's board of directors; SIBUR's latest disclosure (2024) lists Silk Road Fund with 8.5% of SIBUR Holding. Russia's Federal Antimonopoly Service described the acquiring entity as the Silk Road Fund subsidiary 'controlled by the People's Republic of China'.
short: China's state Silk Road Fund holds 8.5% of SIBUR Holding.

source.name: Interfax: SIBUR nearly doubles RAS profit to 166 bln rubles in 9M
source.quote: SIBUR's principal shareholders, according to the latest disclosure, are Leonid Mikhelson with 31%, Gennady Timchenko with 14.45%, China's Sinopec and Silk Road Fund with 8.5% each, Sogaz with 10.625%

additionalSources.name: SIBUR press release: Silk Road Fund successfully closed the Acquisition of a 10% Stake in SIBUR
additionalSources.quote: the shareholders of SIBUR, the largest gas processing and petrochemicals group in Russia, and the Silk Road Fund (SRF), a Chinese investment fund closed the deal on acquisition of 10% equity stake in SIBUR by SRF

additionalSources.name: SIBUR press release: 10% stake in SIBUR to be sold to China's Silk Road Fund
additionalSources.quote: The Silk Road Fund is a financial investor and will have an opportunity to nominate its representative to SIBUR's Board of Directors.

additionalSources.name: TASS: Russia approves Silk Road Fund subsidiary purchasing 10% stake in Sibur
additionalSources.quote: acquisition of a 10% stake in Russian Sibur holding by the Silk Road Fund subsidiary, controlled by the People's Republic of China
